points.quote: `workbench.desktop.main.ts` imports `workbench.common.main.js` (line 15). It then adds the Electron pieces: `./electron-browser/desktop.main.js` and `desktop.contribution.js`, native services such as `nativeTextFileService`
`workbench.web.main.ts` also imports `workbench.common.main.js` (line 16). It then adds `./browser/web.main.js` and browser-only services such as `browserTextFileService`

`src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts` holds everything shared. ... `workbench.desktop.main.ts` imports `workbench.common.main.js` (line 15) ... `workbench.web.main.ts` also imports `workbench.common.main.js` (line 16).
Each platform registers its own implementation of the same service interface, for example the browser versus native text file service ... Shared code depends only on the interface.
a feature's code is loaded only if one of them imports it.
If no entry point imports a `*.contribution.ts` file, it is never bundled or run.
